assumptions.proposition: Patient has symptomatic cholelithiasis as the primary source of her acute RUQ/epigastric pain with radiation to the back
evidence: hx of recurrent symptomatic cholelithiasis with acute abdominal pain. Pain began at 0200, was epigastric in location then moved to the RUQ with radiation to the back
most tender in RUQ. ___ elicits pain but not inspiratory arrest

assumptions.proposition: Acute cholecystitis (rather than uncomplicated biliary colic) is a possible complication given the clinical presentation
evidence: Pain began at 0200, was epigastric in location then moved to the RUQ with radiation to the back. Pain was associated with nausea, vomiting x3
White Blood Cells: 11.3 K/uL (ref 4.0-11.0); Neutrophils: 85.8 % (ref 50.0-70.0)

assumptions.proposition: Biliary obstruction (choledocholithiasis) is not currently supported by laboratory values
evidence: Bilirubin, Total: 0.5 mg/dL (ref 0.0-1.5)
Alkaline Phosphatase: 55.0 IU/L (ref 35.0-105.0); Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT): 40.0 IU/L

assumptions.proposition: Pancreatitis is unlikely as the cause of pain given normal lipase
evidence: Lipase: 44.0 IU/L (ref 0.0-60.0)

assumptions.proposition: Cardiopulmonary and free perforation causes of acute abdominal pain are excluded by chest radiograph
evidence: There is no focal consolidation, effusion, or pneumothorax. The cardiomediastinal silhouette is normal.
No free air below the right hemidiaphragm is seen.

answer_requirements.why_required: Confirms or refutes the primary suspected diagnosis of cholelithiasis

coverage.aggregate_reason: Laboratory and chest radiograph narrow the differential but cannot confirm or characterize gallbladder pathology; direct biliary imaging is required.

current_order_fit.why_this_order_could_answer: Right upper quadrant ultrasound is the first-line modality for gallstone detection and acute cholecystitis assessment, providing real-time evaluation of gallbladder wall, lumen, pericholecystic space, and CBD diameter.
current_order_fit.unsupported_residual: Ultrasound may be limited by body habitus or bowel gas; if non-diagnostic, further imaging (HIDA scan or MRCP) may be needed. The mild chest pain attributed to GERD is not addressed by this order.

parsed.alternative_reconstruction: The mild leukocytosis and neutrophilia combined with RUQ pain could represent early hepatitis or a hepatic abscess rather than primary gallbladder disease; the ultrasound could be ordered primarily to evaluate hepatic parenchyma with gallbladder assessment as secondary, though the known cholelithiasis history makes biliary disease the dominant frame.
